item.title: Tibet House Benefit at Carnegie Hall
item.description: Tibet House Benefit at Carnegie HallMarch 3. 7:30PM. $51-$200 Every year for 39 years, Philip Glass and friends have presented a benefit concert for Tibet House at Carnegie Hall. This annual event supports Tibet House US, a cultural organization founded to support and protect Tibetan culture, and over the years it’s attracted the biggest names in pop, rock, and contemporary classical music. item.title: Kettle Chips: Cameron Healy. The Wild Bet That Made a Brand
item.description: Kettle Chips: Cameron Healy. The Wild Bet That Made a BrandMost founders expand the “right” way: local → regional → national → international.Cameron Healy totally skipped the “national” part. item.title: Anton Batagov at Klavierhaus
item.description: Anton Batagov: Selected Letters of Sergei Rachmaninoff at KlavierhausMar. 4, 8PM Sergei Rachmaninoff, the great 20th century Russian composer, is buried just north of New York, in Westchester County. Pianist and composer Anton Batagov, after visiting Rachmaninoff’s grave, began wondering what the earlier composer might have thought about today’s music. item.title: Wet at National Sawdust
item.description: Wet at National SawdustMarch 5 (The shows on March 6-7 are SOLD OUT) The New York indie-pop group Wet burst onto the scene with their debut album in 2016, led by the sometimes melancholic, sometimes bright songwriting of vocalist Kelly Zutrau. item.title: Sullivan Fortner Trio at Miller Theater
item.description: Sullivan Fortner Trio at Miller TheaterMarch 7. 7:30PM. $12.50-$44.00 Pianist Sullivan Fortner’s career began in New Orleans but is now centered here in NY, where he leads his own trio. He played in the late trumpeter Roy Hargrove’s band, and worked with singers Cecile McLorin Salvant, Samara Joy, and Paul Simon.
